_README: SINGLE SOURCE OF WORKBOOK SHAPE KNOWLEDGE for the price-book -> estimator import.
This file is the ONLY place that records which tabs, which columns and which Rate Config
cells the pipeline expects to find in price-book.xlsx. Both the Python extractor
(extract_workbook.py) and the TypeScript importer (importPriceBook.ts) read it. When a
scheduled price-book run flags 'IMPORT MAPPING IMPACT' (see projects/electrical-price-book.md
SS 'THE WORKBOOK NOW FEEDS SOFTWARE', duty 2), THIS FILE is what gets updated -- so a shape
change is one reviewable diff instead of a hunt through code.
VALIDATION CONTRACT: every column listed below is matched by HEADER TEXT at its stated column
letter, after whitespace normalisation. A missing tab, a renamed header, or a header that has
moved to a different letter ABORTS the import naming exactly what was expected and what was
found. The importer never guesses a column by position and never partially imports.
WHY HEADER TEXT AND NOT POSITION: the 2026-08-09 residential/commercial split proved that
shape changes in this workbook can repoint formulas WITHOUT producing an Excel error. A
position-only mapping would silently mis-map under exactly that failure.
Workbook observed: price-book.xlsx, 2026-08-11, 310 atomics / 43 assemblies (31 residential,

columns.D: Assembly scope rule for this category

rateConfig._note: Each key asserts the LABEL text at that row before the value is read. A moved label aborts the import -- reading B2 without checking A2 is how a re-laid-out sheet silently becomes a wrong labour rate.

_note: Transcribed from the workbook's own formulas on 2026-08-11. The app must reproduce these
EXACTLY -- no rounding differences, no added logic. Each rule names the workbook cell it
was read from so a future reader can re-verify it against the source rather than trusting

supplierUnitCost.meaning: Price as Printed divided down to a per-unit cost; /c = per hundred, /m = per thousand, otherwise divide by Pack Qty.

quotableKey.meaning: Blank on every non-quotable row. This blank is the STRUCTURAL quarantine -- a non-quotable price cannot be matched, so it cannot reach a quote.

costBasisUsed.meaning: Look up this atomic's unit cost at the ACTIVE SUPPLIER only. NO FALLBACK to another supplier. If the active supplier does not carry the item, the basis is BLANK and the assembly reads incomplete -- intentional, per Kyle 2026-08-08.

sellPricePerUnit.meaning: Cost basis multiplied by the markup tier for its own cost band. Blank cost basis => blank sell price, never zero.

assemblyMaterialCost.meaning: N() coerces a blank/text cost basis to 0. An unpriced component therefore contributes ZERO to the cost while the Components Unpriced counter flags it. The counter -- NOT the total -- is what says the number is incomplete.

assemblyLaborHoursAdjusted.meaning: Kyle 2026-08-11: difficulty is a FIELD OBSERVATION. Adjusted hours now equal Total Labor Normal; the prior graded formula is preserved in column AP and is NOT used.

assemblyJobAdderHours.meaning: LEFT(...,2)="NO" is the workbook's own test -- the cells read 'NO - MANUALLY ADDED BY USER WHEN REQUIRED'. Reproduce the two-character test exactly, do not re-interpret it as a boolean.

assemblyPermitFee.meaning: Rate Config B7 is currently BLANK. S adds it only via IF(ISNUMBER(R),R,0), so a blank permit fee contributes nothing rather than erroring.

_note: HOW THE COMPONENT LIST IS DERIVED, AND WHY IT IS NOT TAKEN FROM COLUMN E.
Column E ('Component Item IDs + Qty Formula') is human prose. It also carries
'OUT OF THIS ROW - FIELD-MEASURED' and 'WALKTHROUGH-COUNTED' blocks listing atomics that are
deliberately NOT in the assembly. Parsing E would re-import the very components Kyle's
The authoritative machine-readable component list is the MATERIAL COST FORMULA in column N,
which is what the workbook itself computes from: a sum of `<qty> * N(Atomics!K<row>)` terms.
Atomics are referenced BY ROW NUMBER, so the extractor resolves row -> Item ID against the
Atomics sheet in the same read.
SHAPE HAZARD, RECORDED DELIBERATELY: because these are row references and not Item IDs, any
row insert or delete on the Atomics tab silently repoints every assembly beneath it with no
Excel error. The extractor therefore records both the row number and the resolved Item ID,
and the importer fails loudly if a referenced row is empty or out of range.
componentExtraction.crossCheck: The component set and quantities parsed from N must match those parsed from O exactly. A mismatch means cost and sell are reading different components -- the 2026-08-05 'frozen literal' defect class -- and aborts the import.

knownStructuralFacts._note: Facts about the workbook that the pipeline depends on and that a future run must not quietly change. Each is asserted at import time.

assemblyLaborIsFrozenLiteral.observed: 2026-08-11: 0 of 43 assembly labour formulas (column F) reference the Atomics tab. Every one is literal arithmetic, e.g. '=4*0.25+4*0.05+(4/100)*30+(4/100)*10'.
assemblyLaborIsFrozenLiteral.consequence: Assembly labour does NOT track atomic labour. Changing an atomic's Labor Normal moves nothing in any assembly. Material IS live-linked; labour is not.
assemblyLaborIsFrozenLiteral.pipelineBehaviour: Import the workbook's labour total verbatim so parity holds, and report the atomic-derived comparison separately as a FINDING. The pipeline does not 'fix' this -- it is Kyle's number and his call.

labourTermsNotAttributable.observed: Labour formula term counts frequently differ from component counts (AS-013: 3 labour terms, 2 components; AS-021: 5 labour terms, 3 components).
labourTermsNotAttributable.consequence: Individual labour terms CANNOT be attributed to specific atomics without guessing. The pipeline does not attempt it.

noCachedFormulaValues.observed: 2026-08-11: 3117 formula cells, 0 carrying a cached value. The workbook was last written by openpyxl, which does not calculate.
noCachedFormulaValues.consequence: The workbook's own computed totals cannot be read from the file. The extractor obtains them by recalculating a TEMPORARY COPY in Excel; the live file is only ever read.
